corrected_text_final: At 28.5 °C [T = 28.5 °C], field surveys across the Great Barrier Reef reveal that Thumbprint emperor individuals attain a total length of 19.5 cm [Lp = 19.5 cm] at the onset of gonadal maturation, a size threshold marking the transition to the pubertal stage. Correspondingly, the estimated wet weight at this developmental milestone is 105.8 grams [Wwp = 105.8 grams], a value derived from length-weight relationships established for this species. This body mass at puberty is modest relative to the ultimate wet weight of 2312 grams [Wwi = 2312 grams] achieved by fully grown adults, reflecting a prolonged period of somatic expansion following sexual maturation. The gonadosomatic index (GSI), measured at 11% [GSI = 11%], was recorded under the stable thermal conditions of 28.5 °C [T = 28.5 °C]. Mature females are observed to produce multiple clutches per spawning season, with each event yielding a substantial number of fertilised ova. Newly hatched larvae emerge at a wet weight of approximately 0.00018 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.00018 grams], reflecting the minute pelagic eggs typical of the genus, and field surveys indicate that the ultimate total length attained by the largest adults reaches 54.9 cm [Li = 54.9 cm], with a maximum recorded lifespan of approximately 5475 days [am = approximately 5475 days] at a temperature of 28.5 °C [T = 28.5 °C].
